subject: Residency, TTL & Deletion Controls — Marketplace integration Q&A

Subject: Residency & deletion controls for Nimbus listing — initial questions

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for taking time to kick off the Marketplace integration conversation. As we scope the listing with our platform teams (AWS/GCP/Azure), a few residency / retention / deletion items came up that we need clarified before the SOW: 

- Can Redwood guarantee regional storage of telemetry and customer payloads per marketplace region (US/EU/APAC)? Which deployment option is required (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) to achieve region-locked storage?
- How does Redwood handle retention & TTL for cached KV and prefix caches associated with generation requests? Do customers control TTL per-route?
- For marketplace-driven deletions (e.g., customer exercising data deletion via Nimbus console), what is the expected end-to-end timeline and what logs/evidence do you provide?
- Any constraints if our customers require AWS-resident inference but use GCP listing (we have cross-cloud customers)?

We're gathering these as part of our security/compliance checklist. Happy to join a quick call this week.

Best,
Emily Park
Integration Lead, Nimbus Cloud Marketplace

Emily — thanks, and great questions. Looping in Lauren (product), Ben (partner infra lead), and Priyom (privacy & compliance) so we can answer with the right level of detail. Quick summary up front: we support region-locking via Dedicated or Private deployments; Hosted supports geo-routing with soft residency guarantees and contractual protections. Retention/TTL for caching is configurable by route and we provide audit evidence for deletion workflows. I added a checklist and proposed next steps below.

Proposed next steps:
- Ben: technical note on region-locking and cross-cloud inference options
- Priyom: timeline & evidence for deletion/forensic logs
- Lauren: update SOW template to call out residency options and required customer choices

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai

Cc: Emily Park <emily@cloudnimbus.com>

Subject: RE: Residency & deletion controls for Nimbus listing — technical clarifications

Folks — quick technical breakdown to reference during the call and to attach to the SOW: 

1) Region-locking options:
   - Private (VPC / on-prem): full data residency in customer network — both payloads and logs never leave the specified region (hardware-deployed in-region).
   - Dedicated (Redwood-managed, reserved capacity): can pin GPU pools to cloud region and attach region-specific object storage for model assets and persistent logs — guarantees via the Dedicated contract and SLA.
   - Hosted API: we support routing by region and tenancy but the control plane is multi-region; for strict regulatory residency, Hosted alone is not sufficient unless combined with contractual data locality clauses and encryption-at-rest/key-residency controls.

2) Caching & TTL behavior:
   - Prefix/KV cache: TTL is configurable per route in the Redwood Console (default 24h). Cache entries tied to generation inputs are stored on serving nodes; in Dedicated/Private they live in-region.
   - Forced deletion: API endpoint available to invalidate keys; batch deletion supported via admin job. Deletion is best-effort on hosted but guaranteed in Dedicated/Private within the SLA window.

3) Marketplace deletion flow evidence:
   - When Nimbus submits a customer deletion request via the partner API we: 1) acknowledge request within 4 hours, 2) run safe deletion with integrity checks, 3) provide a deletion receipt (JSON) plus audit log slice showing affected objects and timestamps.
   - Expected E2E timeline: Hosted: up to 72 hours for complete KV eviction and log copy retention purge; Dedicated: SLA-backed 24–48 hours; Private: customer-controlled, immediate once ops run the script.

4) Cross-cloud constraints:
   - We can route inference requests to region-specific endpoints regardless of where a listing appears, but storage and model assets must be provisioned in the target cloud/region to be fully compliant for residency. Cross-cloud inference (control plane in one cloud, data plane in another) is supported, but we flag it in the SOW as an exception and require an explicit architecture sign-off.

I'll attach the rough residency matrix.

— Ben

Emily — attaching an internal-friendly checklist and SOW language draft that we can share with Nimbus legal/ops. Key callouts included in the draft: 

- Required customer decision points for listing: preferred residency mode (Hosted soft-residency vs Dedicated vs Private), required key management (Redwood KMS vs customer KMS/HSM), and allowed cross-cloud inference patterns.
- Clear TTL defaults (24h) and per-route override policy.
- Deletion SLA language with evidence deliverables (deletion receipt + audit log window).

I also added a small paragraph describing the lifecycle of cache entries and recommended best practices for sensitive PII (masking + short TTL).

Attachments: Nimbus-friendly SOW snippet and the residency matrix Ben produced. Please review ahead of the sync.

Thanks — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. A couple follow ups before the call: 

1) For Hosted customers who require EU-only storage for telemetry, can we surface an encryption key residency option (customer-provided key) that guarantees logs are unreadable outside region?
2) On deletion receipts: can the receipt include a hash of deleted objects and an operator ID to satisfy our audit requirements?

Also, our legal wants a one-line fallback in the SOW for scenarios where a Dedicated pool is down and we trigger a temporary cross-region fallback. Can you propose wording that limits exposure and notes automatic re-sync when capacity returns?

We can do the Wed 12/09 10:00 PT sync — invite sent.

Emily
Emily Park
Integration Lead, Nimbus Cloud Marketplace

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: Emily Park <emily@cloudnimbus.com>, aditya_rao@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 08 Dec 2026 16:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Residency, TTL & Deletion Controls — Marketplace integration Q&A

Emily — quick answers to the two follow-ups: 

1) Customer-provided key (bring-your-own-key): yes. For Hosted customers we support envelope encryption where object metadata is stored in our control plane but the symmetric keys are customer-managed in a supported KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault). If the key is in-region and you rotate access, logs and telemetry are effectively unreadable without the key. We will add explicit SOW language to state this as an available option per listing.

2) Deletion receipt fields: we can include: request_id, timestamp, list_of_affected_keys (hashed), operator_id (internal redwood operator UID), and a signed assertion (HMAC) that the deletion job completed. That should meet typical marketplace audit requirements.

3) Fallback wording suggestion for SOW (single sentence): "In the event of sustained Dedicated pool unavailability, Redwood may temporarily route inference requests to alternate region capacity; Redwood will notify Nimbus within one hour of fallback initiation, limit cross-region processing to non-sensitive workloads per agreed classification, and automatically re-synchronize state to the nominated region when original capacity is restored."

We'll include the BYOK option and the receipt schema in the call materials. See also: https://drive.redwood.ai/teams/nimbus/residency_matrix_v1 (matrix & SOW snippet).

— Priyom Das
Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference
